patch_description: Crossover of the two programs: keep the LP-based hill-climb framework from the current program (which yields globally optimal radii for a given center layout), but replace the expensive scipy LP evaluation during the search loop with the fast Gauss-Seidel "water filling" + monotone repair from the second program. This makes each hill-climb iteration ~10x cheaper, letting us afford more iterations while keeping the LP only for the final, exact radius assignment. Additionally, a short deterministic overlap-repulsion refinement pass (from the second program) is run first to spread clusters before random hill-climbing, and the wall-push directed moves are retained. The result should match or exceed 2.45 while cutting runtime.
